claims.claim: The paper draws conceptual analogies between ML uncertainty evaluation and metrology (GUM), distinguishing process-level and result-level quality.
claims.quoted_support: Particular attention is devoted to the distinction between process-level and result-level quality and to the limitations of the conventional classification of ML uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components.

claims.claim: It argues the aleatoric/epistemic dichotomy, like random vs systematic measurement errors, is model-dependent and an insufficient basis for unified uncertainty evaluation.
claims.quoted_support: this dichotomy, similarly to the traditional distinction between random and systematic measurement errors, is inherently model-dependent and provides an insufficient basis for a unified uncertainty evaluation framework.

claims.claim: Generative ML systems are explicitly out of scope.
claims.stance_target: metrology framing already covers LLM confidence
claims.quoted_support: we do not consider here generative ML systems, which would deserve a different treatment
